meta.title: Photography 101 — what makes a photo
meta.description: An interactive guide for non-photographers. Drag a slider and see what aperture, shutter speed, ISO or focal length does to a photo.

intro.title: The scene
intro.body: A head, one key light, a backdrop. One scene turns into a different photo every time, depending on how you set the camera. Scroll down and play with the sliders.

expozice.title: Exposure
expozice.body: Exposure is the total amount of light that reaches the sensor. Too little → a dark photo, too much → blown out. The slider moves exposure in EV; +1 EV means twice the light.

clona.title: Aperture
clona.body: The aperture is the opening in the lens, given as an f-number. A low number (f/1.8) = a wide opening and shallow depth of field: sharp subject, blurred background. A high number (f/16) = deep depth of field, foreground and background both sharp.

cas.title: Shutter speed
cas.body: Shutter speed is how long light keeps falling on the sensor. A short time (1/1000 s) freezes motion, a long one (1/15 s and slower) smears it into a streak. Watch the ball orbiting the head.

iso.title: ISO
iso.body: ISO is the sensor's sensitivity. A higher value brightens the photo when light is scarce, but adds noise (grain). Keep it as low as the light allows.

ohnisko.title: Focal length
ohnisko.body: Focal length (in mm) sets the angle of view. Change focal length and distance together so the subject stays the same size, and perspective changes: a short lens up close stretches the nearest features, a long lens from afar compresses perspective. It sets the relationship between the face and the background.

uhel.title: Camera angle
uhel.body: The camera's height relative to the subject. Shooting from below makes the subject look bigger, from above smaller; eye level is neutral. It's a tool for the mood of the shot, not a rule.

wb.title: White balance
wb.body: White balance tells the camera which light temperature to treat as neutral (in kelvins). A lower value leaves the photo warmer (orange), a higher one cooler (blue). Set it to match the light source.

kompozice.title: Composition
kompozice.body: Where the subject belongs in the frame. Pick a composition and compare how it changes the feel.

svetlo.title: The exposure triangle
svetlo.body: Aperture, shutter speed and ISO don't just change the look. All three also change how much light gets in. Open the aperture and watch the exposure meter below: the photo blows out. Shutter speed and ISO behave the same way.

capstone-blur.title: Balance the exposure: blurred background
capstone-blur.body: You want a blurred background, so the aperture stays nearly wide open. It only closes to f/3.2, or the background would sharpen up. But that lets in a lot of light and the photo is blown out. Lower the shutter speed and ISO (fine-tune with the aperture) until the meter sits at zero.

capstone-freeze.title: Balance the exposure: freeze the motion
capstone-freeze.body: You want to freeze fast motion, so the shutter can't go slower than 1/250 s, or the motion blurs. But a short time lets in little light and the photo is dark. Open the aperture and raise the ISO (fine-tune with the shutter) until the meter sits at zero.

finale.title: I handle all of this for you
finale.body: Now you know how many decisions go into one good photo. I make them for you. You just look into the lens. Tell me what you'd like to shoot.

thirds.label: Thirds
thirds.body: The subject sits on a thirds intersection, not dead centre. The mass in the opposite third counterweights it, so the frame feels balanced rather than static.

center.label: Centred
center.body: The subject exactly in the middle, the background mirrored around it. Formal and direct. It works when you want calm and a straight-on gaze.

golden.label: Golden ratio
golden.body: The 1 : 1.618 proportion painters have used for centuries. The subject sits in the tightest coil of the golden spiral and the lights curl outward along it, so the eye rides the wide arm inward and lands on the face. Against thirds it is not about position, it is about that flow.

leading.label: Leading lines
leading.body: Lines in the frame (paths, edges, light) guide the viewer's eye to the subject. The lights have lined up into two rows that recede into depth and converge right on the face.

space.label: Negative space
space.body: The subject is small and pushed to the edge; the rest of the frame stays empty. Negative space lets the shot breathe and underlines scale.

frame.label: Frame within a frame
frame.body: Out-of-focus foreground wraps the subject and builds a frame around it. The eye has no way in but the hole in the middle, so attention goes exactly where you want it.

foceni101.capstoneWin: You traded one for the other. That's the whole triangle.
